name: KTP Progression
description: Aerial construction-progress record of the KTP data-centre campus: 50 drone frames from five visits, matched into 12 before/after sets and registered into 14 drag-to-compare pairs and 13 transition clips.
method: DJI XMP gives GPS, relative altitude, gimbal yaw and pitch for 32 of 48 obliques; 16 lost it to compression
slant distance = relative_altitude / tan(|pitch|); projected along yaw to a ground target point
single-link clustering of ground targets at 55 m separates the frames into plots
consecutive-frame SIFT + mutual nearest neighbour + MAGSAC homography, composed along each chain
frames ordered by construction stage from the imagery alone, then checked against capture dates
no interpolation or generative synthesis: every pixel is a photograph

frames.note: site-wide overview predating the 2025 sequence; intentionally outside the set matching
no counterpart found in any later visit; intentionally unassigned

comparisons.title: The roof fills up
comparisons.caption: Registered through the 8 October frame in two steps. The red earth and the perimeter road hold perfectly still; everything that moves is plant going onto the roof.

comparisons.title: South elevation
comparisons.caption: The dark facade panels were already hung in October. What changes is the roof filling in and the signage going up.

comparisons.title: Bare slab to full plant
comparisons.caption: The two straight-down camera positions land six metres apart on the ground — the tightest registration in the whole set.

comparisons.title: Roof deck to full plant
comparisons.caption: Sixty-seven days. Bare deck and precast walls on the left, complete rooftop plant and entrance canopy on the right.

comparisons.title: Both halls at once
comparisons.caption: The frame that would not cluster with either hall, because it sits centred between them.

comparisons.title: The plot next door

registration.note: below inlier threshold; presented as a wipe, both frames unmodified

comparisons.caption: Bearings 38° apart and a plot that changed completely — only 8 inlier matches, below the threshold. An honest wipe between two unmodified frames.

comparisons.title: Pile caps to standing frame

registration.note: below inlier threshold; presented as a wipe, both frames unmodified

comparisons.caption: 13 inliers, not enough to trust a homography when almost every feature in the frame was built between the two visits.

comparisons.title: Earthworks to foundations
comparisons.caption: The weakest registration that still passed. Near-featureless bare earth gives the matcher very little to hold on to, but the boundary roads pinned it.

comparisons.title: Podium to roof deck
comparisons.caption: The two finished halls across the road stay locked in place while the frame in front of them grows a roof.

comparisons.title: Canal-side block
comparisons.caption: The canal at the left edge is what identified this block, and it is also what anchors the registration.

comparisons.title: Second block
comparisons.caption: Precast planks across an open frame become a topped deck carrying plant steel.

comparisons.title: Both blocks from above
comparisons.caption: These two frames were shot 169° apart in gimbal yaw. The homography puts them back on top of each other.

comparisons.title: The admin building
comparisons.caption: A control. Slide it and almost nothing moves except a few parked cars — which is how you know the method is not inventing change.

comparisons.title: East halls in service
comparisons.caption: The slight shift at the divider is parallax on a tall building, not construction.
